newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania sets tender for transport firms.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania sets tender for transport firms.

text.p: Lithuania on Friday invited bids from local and international financial advisors to draw up privatisation plans for two port handling companies and a shipping firm.

"The government anounces today a tender to draw up a privatisation programme for Klaipeda Stevedoring Company (KLASCO), Klaipedos Smelte and Klaipeda Sea shipping company (LISCO)," the deputy head of the privatisation department at the European Affairs ministry, Alfredas Ramanauskas, told Reuters.
Ramanauskas said applications for the tender are expected before July 11.
"Then we will draw up a short list and give them another 30 days to submit the proposals," Ramanauskas added.
He said the winner of the bid to draw up a privatisation plan for the transport companies would be chosen by end August and the privatisation would begin six to nine months after.
He said two advisors would be chosen: one for KLASCO and Smelte and the other for LISCO.
KLASCO is Lithuania's biggest stevedoring company, which handles around seven million tonnes of cargo per year. The firm is 90 percent state-run. A ferry terminal is an integral part of the company.
Klaipedos Smelte is 89.5 state owned and handles around one million tonnes of cargo per year.
The state owns 80 percent of LISCO, a company with 38 vessels and two ferries for passengers and cargos.
The firms are part of a list of key companies that the government has decided to privatise, including the airline, telecommunications firm and two state banks.
